steps.content: Starting with a standard configuration for Random Forest will allow us to establish a baseline for performance.

The Random Forest model achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.95731 with a standard deviation of 0.01709. The validation accuracy is 0.94152. This is a strong baseline, but I will continue to experiment to see if I can improve on this performance.
Increasing the number of estimators and adjusting the maximum depth may enhance the model's performance.

The updated Random Forest model with 150 estimators and a max depth of 12 achieved a mean cross-validated accuracy of 0.96231, which is an improvement over the previous configuration. The validation accuracy also improved to 0.94737. I will continue experimenting to explore further enhancements.
Tweaking the maximum depth further while increasing the number of estimators could yield even better performance.

The model with 200 estimators and a max depth of 14 did not improve upon the previous best mean accuracy of 0.96231, nor did it increase the validation accuracy. Therefore, no significant gain was achieved with this configuration. I will stop here and recommend the last configuration as the best.

steps.final_recommendation: Random Forest with 150 estimators and max depth of 12 (mean CV accuracy: 0.96231, val accuracy: 0.94737) is the best-performing model.
